newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish c.bank backs decision to free fuel prices.
newsitem.headline: Polish c.bank backs decision to free fuel prices.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland's deputy president Witold Kozinski on Thursday said that the government's decision to free fuel prices was correct.
"I generally think that the decision (to liberalise fuel prices) was correct. It had to be done," Kozinski told Reuters.
Kozinski also said that despite possible increases in fuel prices in the short-term, the move was unlikely to affect the central bank's present monetary policy.

The central bank has said that it intends to keep a tight monetary policy in 1997 to help bring down inflation to the planned target of 13 percent year-on-year at the end of 1997 from 18.5 percent last December.

Kozinski also said the central bank's recent decision to increase obligatory reserves for commercial banks did not harm the economy, because banks had so far made only minute changes in deposit and credit rates.
"These micro-changes in credit and deposit rates show that the increase...did not harm the economy," Kozinski said.

Last month the central bank said it would increase obligatory reserves on zloty call deposits by three points to 20 percent and currency deposits by two points to four percent starting from Febrauary 28.
On Wednesday state-owned Pekao SA bank said it would raise the base zloty credit rate by 0.5 point to 25 percent and cut interest on zloty deposits by between one and two points.
